title: ID and OOD Performance Are Sometimes Inversely Correlated on Real-world Datasets

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models on in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets containing known spurious features (e.g., image backgrounds in Waterbirds, hospital domains in Camelyon17) to measure whether ID accuracy trades off inversely with OOD generalization.

Measuring worst-group accuracy on the CivilComments dataset to evaluate model performance across subpopulations defined by combinations of toxicity labels and spuriously associated demographic attributes (e.g., male, Christian, LGBT).
